meta.title: Bengali Alphabet (Bangla script)
meta.subtitle: 56 letters and signs · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The Bengali script (Bangla lipi) in which Bengali is written: 56 notes, in the traditional order — the eleven vowels, the five signs that sit on or beside them, the consonants row by row, the three dotted letters (ড়, ঢ়, য়), the two joined letters every primer teaches with the alphabet (ক্ষ, জ্ঞ) and the three phola signs (য-ফলা, র-ফলা, ব-ফলা) met on almost every page. The first deck of the Bengali collection. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Each vowel is shown alone and as the sign it becomes after a consonant, written on ক (আ · কা), since the sign is what a reader meets most. Every note gives the romanisation the level decks use, the sound described in English words, and one everyday word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them. Bengali spelling keeps distinctions its speech has lost — ই and ঈ are one sound, as are উ and ঊ, শ and ষ, ন and ণ — and the cards say so; where English has no equivalent — the breathy consonants (kh, gh, bh …), the turned-back retroflex row (ṭ, ḍ) against the soft dental t and d — the card says what to do with the tongue or the breath instead. Sources: the standard description of Standard Colloquial Bengali; the example words' romanisations are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: অ
fields.Sound: ô · an open "o", like the o of British hot; every consonant carries it unless a sign says otherwise, so it has no sign of its own — and at the end of most words it is not said at all (নাম is nam)

fields.Name: আ
fields.Sound: a · "a" as in father, but short — Bengali has no long vowels

fields.Name: ই
fields.Sound: i · "i", between the i of bit and the ee of see; its sign is written BEFORE the consonant it follows in speech

fields.Name: ঈ
fields.Sound: i · said exactly like ই — the "long i" survives only in spelling, mostly in words from Sanskrit

fields.Name: উ
fields.Sound: u · "u", between the u of put and the oo of food

fields.Name: ঊ
fields.Sound: u · said exactly like উ — the "long u" survives only in spelling

fields.Name: ঋ
fields.Sound: ri · said "ri" as in rip; found in words from Sanskrit

fields.Name: এ
fields.Sound: e · like the a of cake, without the glide into "ee" — or, in many words, like the a of cat (এক is said æk)

fields.Name: ঐ
fields.Sound: ōi · "oi" as in boy

fields.Name: ও
fields.Sound: ō · like the o of go, but one pure vowel, without the glide into "oo"

fields.Name: ঔ
fields.Sound: ōu · "o" gliding into "u", like the ow of low said slowly

fields.Name: অনুস্বার
fields.Sound: ṅ · anusvar, the small circle after the letter: "ng" as in sing

fields.Name: বিসর্গ
fields.Sound: ḥ · bisorgo, the two dots: inside a word it doubles the consonant after it (দুঃখ is said dukkho); rare

fields.Name: চন্দ্রবিন্দু
fields.Sound: chondrobindu, the moon and dot above: the vowel is said through the nose, as in French bon

fields.Name: হসন্ত
fields.Sound: hoshonto, the stroke below: the consonant has NO vowel after it; usually two such consonants are joined into one shape instead (ক্ + ত = ক্ত)

fields.Name: খণ্ড ত
fields.Sound: t · khondo to, "half t": a t with no vowel after it, closing a syllable

fields.Name: ক
fields.Sound: kô · "k" as in skin — no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: খ
fields.Sound: khô · "k" with a strong puff of breath, as in kit said firmly

fields.Name: গ
fields.Sound: gô · "g" as in go

fields.Name: ঘ
fields.Sound: ghô · "g" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of doghouse

fields.Name: ঙ
fields.Sound: ṅô · "ng" as in sing; never starts a word

fields.Name: চ
fields.Sound: cô · "ch" as in church, but with no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: ছ
fields.Sound: chô · "ch" with a strong puff of breath, as in the middle of church-hill

fields.Name: জ
fields.Sound: jô · "j" as in jam

fields.Name: ঝ
fields.Sound: jhô · "j" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of hedgehog

fields.Name: ঞ
fields.Sound: ñô · said as a plain "n", and found almost only joined to চ or জ (ঞ্চ, ঞ্জ)

fields.Name: ট
fields.Sound: ṭô · a "t" made with the tip of the tongue turned up behind the gum ridge (retroflex); the nearest English sound is the t of top

fields.Name: ঠ
fields.Sound: ṭhô · the turned-back (retroflex) t, with a strong puff of breath

fields.Name: ড
fields.Sound: ḍô · a "d" made with the tongue tip turned up behind the gum ridge (retroflex); the nearest English sound is the d of dog

fields.Name: ঢ
fields.Sound: ḍhô · the turned-back (retroflex) d, followed by a breathy h

fields.Name: ণ
fields.Sound: ṇô · written in words from Sanskrit, but said exactly like ন, a plain "n"

fields.Name: ত
fields.Sound: tô · a soft "t" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth (dental), as in French or Spanish; no puff of breath

fields.Name: থ
fields.Sound: thô · the dental t with a strong puff of breath — not the "th" of thin

fields.Name: দ
fields.Sound: dô · a soft "d" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth (dental) — not the "th" of this

fields.Name: ধ
fields.Sound: dhô · the dental d followed by a breathy h

fields.Name: ন
fields.Sound: nô · "n" as in no

fields.Name: প
fields.Sound: pô · "p" as in spin — no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: ফ
fields.Sound: phô · "p" with a strong puff of breath; many speakers say it as "f"

fields.Name: ব
fields.Sound: bô · "b" as in bat

fields.Name: ভ
fields.Sound: bhô · "b" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of clubhouse; some speakers say it nearly as "v"

fields.Name: ম
fields.Sound: mô · "m" as in man

fields.Name: য
fields.Sound: jô · said like জ, a "j" as in jam, at the start of a word; joined after a consonant it is the য-ফলা below

fields.Name: র
fields.Sound: rô · a tapped "r", one flick of the tongue, as in Spanish pero

fields.Name: ল
fields.Sound: lô · "l" as in leaf, said with the tongue forward

fields.Name: শ
fields.Sound: śô · "sh" as in ship

fields.Name: ষ
fields.Sound: ṣô · a second "sh", written in words from Sanskrit; said just like শ

fields.Name: স
fields.Sound: śô · usually a third "sh", like শ — but a true "s" as in sun before ত, থ, ন, র, ল and in English words (স্কুল, school)

fields.Name: হ
fields.Sound: hô · "h" as in hand

fields.Name: ড়
fields.Sound: ṛô · a flap: the tongue tip turns back and flicks forward against the roof of the mouth, a sound between d and r; never starts a word

fields.Name: ঢ়
fields.Sound: ṛhô · the same flap with a breath of h after it, in a few words from Sanskrit; most speakers say it just like ড়

fields.Name: য়
fields.Sound: ẏô · a glide between vowels, "y" as in yes or "w" as in we, by the vowels around it (খাওয়া is said khawa)

fields.Name: ক্ষ
fields.Sound: kkhô · a joined letter, ক্ + ষ: said "kh" at the start of a word and "kkh" inside one (পরীক্ষা, porikkha)

fields.Name: জ্ঞ
fields.Sound: ggô · a joined letter, জ্ + ঞ: said "g" at the start of a word, the vowel after it turned to æ and nasal (জ্ঞান is said gæn), and "gg" inside one

fields.Name: য-ফলা
fields.Sound: jo-phola, the hook after a consonant: inside a word it doubles the consonant; at the start it turns a following a into æ (ব্যথা is said bætha)

fields.Name: র-ফলা
fields.Sound: ro-phola, the stroke below: an "r" straight after the consonant, as in pr, tr, kr

fields.Name: ব-ফলা
fields.Sound: bo-phola, the small ব below: inside a word it doubles the consonant (বিশ্বাস is said bishshash); at the start it is silent
